description: What the SPA served by the local Python server is allowed to ask the shell for. The `default` capability deliberately leaves IPC inert on that origin, so each entry here is opened deliberately and kept minimal. start_dragging / internal_toggle_maximize: with an Overlay titlebar the webview covers the whole title area, so macOS offers no draggable strip of its own and the page must nominate one with data-tauri-drag-region — which Tauri implements over IPC. opener:allow-open-url: opens a link in the user's own browser, so the 'Star on GitHub' link does not navigate the app itself out of the library. The two map entries are the 'Open in Maps' button beside a photo's coordinates: Smriti fetches no map tiles — a tile request would hand the photo's location to someone else's server — so street-level detail is something only another app can offer, and this hands the coordinates over on a deliberate click. Apple Maps on a Mac, OpenStreetMap in the browser elsewhere. Both are exact patterns, not a general opener. allow-updates + core:event:allow-listen: the update notice now lives in the app itself rather than in a native dialog, which opens as a window — or, on a Mac set to prefer tabs, a tab — of its own, detached from the app it is about and easily missed behind it. So the page must be able to ask what the updater found, accept an update, and hear download progress while it runs. Listening is receive-only: the page can hear the shell's events, it cannot emit any. allow-pick-folder: raises the system folder chooser and returns the path the user picked, for the two places a folder is chosen — adding a library folder, and choosing where a Takeout import should land. Its own command rather than dialog:allow-open, which would let the page raise any file dialog it liked. The whole surface is moving the window, opening a URL, updating, and asking for a folder.
